stage1.impression: Clean night-time quay with a glowing ring sculpture, a lamp post, bollards and lit canal houses. At 1:1 it still reads as CG. The rims look like neon tubes rather than the edges of thick acrylic discs, and the clear faces don't show at all. The whole frame sits in one amber cast, the house facades repeat a flat grid of windows, and the coloured shadow, which is the point of this frame, is a faint, muddy wash. A jury would see a nice render of a specific object, but not yet a photograph of a striking work in a real Amsterdam place. (Note: the critic prompt describes a listening-bar interior, but this image and its card are an outdoor light-festival entry, so I judged it as a night photograph against the card's purpose.)

blocking_9: The coloured shadow must read at a glance as the globe drawn in saturated coloured light: the shadow patches clearly coloured and clearly darker or brighter than the lit paving, not a 55-vs-83 luminance wash that is almost all brown
The discs must read as thick cast acrylic, with the faces catching the spot as faint clear sheets and reflections, not as bare neon hoops
Neutral grey-white balance on stone and paving, so the rims' six colours aren't the only non-amber values in the frame (paving b_median is now 12 to 23)
Canal houses with real Amsterdam facade variety (gables, brick texture, uneven window lighting, curtains), not one repeated window grid
Plinth and dark areas need detail; the plinth now has a lum_median of 10
Some sign of life or scale: a person or a bicycle in the middle distance

defects.what: Coloured shadow is low-contrast and desaturated. Its median luminance is 55 against 83 for the lit paving beside it, the colours are muddy browns and mauves, and the edge is soft (44 px from 10 to 90 %) for a hard spot
Rims read as neon tube hoops. The disc faces are invisible, so nothing says thick acrylic. 1.24 % of the globe region is clipped
Plinth is crushed to near-black (lum_median 10) with no sheen or edge on the blackened steel
Houses across the canal are a uniform repeated window grid with flat emissive panes and flat brick, which reads as a game backdrop
Overall amber cast. Paving B channel median is 12 to 16, so the stone has no neutral grey
Street lamp head is blown with a haze bloom (clip 0.38 %)
Water is a dark, flat sheet with streak reflections only. There is no separation between the far quay wall and the water
Rusty bollards are identical generic copies

changes.problem: The hard spot is too weak and too warm for the coloured shadow to read, and that shadow is what this frame is for.

evidence.measured: shadow lum_median 54.4 vs lit paving [700,580,950,660] 83.7; shadow RGB median 87/48/23 (brown); edge width 44 px

change.to: 900 W, 4200 K, cone 16 deg (keep the aim)

changes.expected: Lit paving in the spot around 120, the shadow's coloured patches clearly tinted (red, blue and yellow distinguishable) and sharper edged

changes.problem: The whole frame is amber, so the paving and stone have no neutral and the globe's colours lose their contrast.
changes.expected: Paving turns warm grey instead of orange; the sodium-warm lamps stay warm but the stone reads neutral

changes.problem: The rims clip and read as neon tubes. With the spot this weak, nothing reveals the clear faces of the discs.

change.setting: the globe: the rims' glow (emission strength)
change.to: 0.13 (with c1, the stronger spot catches the faces and edges)

changes.expected: Rims glow saturated without clipping; the faces show faint spot highlights and reflections of the houses, so they read as thick acrylic

changes.problem: The blackened-steel plinth is crushed to a featureless black hole under the hero.

change.to: 1.0 W/m2 at 3200 K; plinth finish given a soft satin sheen (paving/quay material finish)

changes.expected: Plinth reads as dark steel with a soft rim highlight on its top edge, median around 20

changes.problem: The canal houses are a repeated window grid with flat glowing panes, which gives away the render.

evidence.measured: seen: identical window sizes and spacing, uniform pane colours, flat brick

change.setting: the houses across: lit windows and brick finish
change.to: 0.25 lit with per-window glow randomised 0.03 to 0.12 and colour 2400 to 3500 K, curtains or interiors behind some panes, brick bump and mortar, varied gables

changes.expected: The far bank reads as real Amsterdam canal houses; the windows' p95 drops and their variety rises

changes.problem: The water and far quay merge into a dark slab with no horizon or separation.

change.to: 0.12 with a cool blue-grey night gradient; finer ripple so the reflections break into dashes

changes.expected: The water carries a faint cool sky sheen and broken reflections; the far quay's edge separates

changes.problem: The near street lamp is blown and blooms into the haze.
changes.expected: The lamp head holds a bright core with no clipped halo

changes.problem: Nothing gives scale or life; the identical rusty bollards read as stock models.

evidence.measured: seen: two identical bollards, an empty quay

change.to: Amsterdam black steel 'Amsterdammertje' bollards with varied wear; a parked bicycle against the far-left railing and one blurred person 6 to 10 m off near the lamp

changes.expected: The 2 m scale reads instantly, and the place reads as Amsterdam

out_of_scope.request: Make the disc faces visibly tinted, not only the rims, so the globe reads as solid coloured acrylic
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes rim-lit discs with clear faces

out_of_scope.request: Thicken the discs to read as more substantial acrylic
out_of_scope.why: The 25 mm disc thickness is fixed
